sources.evidence: The page is titled Championship Round Results (1998-9) and ends with Last updated October 26, 1998, which fits the 1998 edition (nena-1998), not 1997.

nena-1998.notes: Source 6 (RIT_1998.pdf) is a problem set of six other problems, probably a preliminary-site set, with no contest name in the document. Source 1: the home page link text says results for 1997-1998 but the page it leads to is titled 1998-9. The crawl holds the 1999-2000 regional rules page.

sources.evidence: The home page is titled ACM Northeast North America Region Home Page and links to the 1998-1999 sites and dates pages, which give the regional final as October 24, 1998 at Westfield State College.
The page is titled ACM Northeast North America Championship Round Results (1998-9), shows a grid of 12 teams, and was last updated October 26, 1998.
The page has the same title and the same 12-row table as source 2.
The page is headed North East North American Regionals 1998 and links to problems.pdf.
The PDF starts with the title 1998 Northeast North America Programming Contest followed by Problem Number 1: The Return of the Roman Empire.

The PDF holds six problems (Where are we?, Who is on first?, Y2K, Bits and bits and bits and ..., Back to BASIC?, In, Out, or on the Edge?) that are not the six of the regional final's set, and it names no contest.
The listing is headed Regionals 1998 :: North America - Northeast NA and has six problems, numbered 5335 to 5340, whose titles are those of source 5.

nena-1999.notes: Source 6 (RIT_1999.pdf) has the same six problems as the 1998 regional set (nena-1998 source 5), with its title line missing. Source 1 is a snapshot of April 2000 whose home page lists 2000-2001 sites and dates (all TBA) beside the 1999-2000 results.

sources.evidence: The home page is titled ACM Northeast North America Region Home Page and links to the 1999-2000 results page, the regional rules and the Westfield State College site pages.
The page is headed Northeast North America ACM Programming Contest Final Standings: 1999-2000 and shows 13 team rows with seven problem columns each; it was last updated November 8, 1999.
The page has the same heading and the same 13-row table as source 2.
The page is headed North East North American Regionals 1999 and links to problems.pdf.

The PDF opens with the heading Northeast Regional Championship Round of the 1999-2000 ACM International Collegiate Programming Contest, Westfield State College, November 6, 1999, and seven problems #1 to #7.
The PDF has six problems, The Return of the Roman Empire to Pentominos, whose text matches the 1998 regional set (nena-1998) and none of the seven 1999 problems from Cubism to Cell growth.

nena-2000.notes: Final day conflicts inside the copies: the rules page says Nov. 4, the dates page, the standings and the Baylor page say Nov. 6. Source 6 (RIT_2000.pdf) names no contest; it is taken as the Western Preliminary (RIT, Oct 21 2000) problem set because it has 7 problems like the RIT preliminary scoreboard in source 1, and not as a regional final set; check if a preliminary-site problem set counts as a problemset of the contest.
